headers.title: Virtual Transcription Laboratory
headers.description: Virtual Transcription Laboratory is a tool that allows you to create digital text based on scans. The results can be used to prepare a digital object in standards such as: hOCR, TEI, PDF, eBook. The tool allows the transcription of objects imported from Digital Libraries, also using the IIIF standard.

howToStart.title: How to start transcribing?
howToStart.desc: To transcribe pages in the Virtual Transcription Laboratory you must:

step.step1desc: After registration, a message containing a link to activate the account will be sent to the e-mail address provided in the form. Click on it or copy it to the browsers address bar. The activation link is valid for limited time.
step.step3title: to start, select from the main menu option
step.step3desc: Enter the data one by one or import the object description with files from an external source. After entering the data, accept the regulations and confirm the completion of the transcription description by clicking the Create new transcription button.
step.step4title: Enter a description of the new transcription, accept the terms and then click "Create a new transcription"
step.step4desc: After clicking "Create a new transcription", a message will appear on the screen saying that you have successfully created a new transcription. You are now automatically on the page with the new transcription and you can add the pages of this transcription to be transcribed.
step.step5title: The new transcription will appear on the screen immediately. You can now add pages to transcribe.
step.step5desc: Every transcription you create is located in the Transcripts / My Transcriptions tab. You must be logged in to view the My Transcriptions page . By default, the newly created transcription is not available to other Adiadna users, both logged in and not logged in.
step.step6title: If you want your transcription to be visible to other users, go to the Permissions tab on the My transcription page
step.step7title: After adding transcription pages, you can start automatically transcribing all added pages, or you can transcribe each file individually.
step.step7desc: If you want to automatically transcribe each page separately, first click on the page tile. A new window will open for transcribing the page you selected, one of the options is "Automatic transcription" of the visible page. The Automatically transcribe option is one of the most important tools available in VTL. Otherwise it is called OCR (Optical Character Recognition) or optical character recognition on a document scan. It can be said that OCR extracts text from an image.
step.step8title: Click the selected page and go to the transcription window.
step.readMore: After creating a new transcription and adding transcription pages to it, you can start working with the file. To do this, click on the selected page. The selected page will appear in a new window with all the tools you need to transcribe the page file. If you want to know how to work with a file on the transcription page, read on
step.step2desc: After completing the registration form, you will receive a link to the e-mail address provided, after clicking on which you activate your account. It will then be possible to log in - using the data provided during account registration.
step.step6desc: From now on, you can start working with the text, which you can proceed to alone or with a team. Add project participants by clicking on the "Participants" option and assign them a role in the project. The scope of permissions depends on the role assigned:
step.endDesc1: - has full possibilities of editing text layers,
step.endDesc2: - in addition to the participant's rights, it also has the ability to moderate, i.e. accept and reject changes made in text layers by users with the role of "participant", including their own changes,
step.endDesc3: - has full capabilities of project management, moderation of changes and editing text layers.

howToTranscribe.title: How to transcribe?
howToTranscribe.desc: Description of tools and how to work with the file on the transcription window page.

section.workOnWindow: Work on a window with a transcribed object
section.workOnWindowDescription: Description of the operation of the transcribed object window tools
section.workWithWindowDescription: Click on the line ruler you want to transcribe. The verse will be highlighted. The blue frame of the edited line appears in both the transcribed object view and the transcription view. Thanks to this you will be able to see on the transcribed object which page row you are editing.

steps.step1desc: Automatic transcription not only translates all verses or paragraphs of the page again. You can automatically transcribe only verses that have not yet been transcribed. You can define such settings after clicking the „Automatically transcribe” button.
steps.step2desc: You can collapse the transcription window and view the entire page of the transcribed object or vice versa. To do this, click the "Collapse" button, because again see both windows click "Expand".
steps.step3desc: This feature allows you to swap pages with the transcription of the transcribed object.
steps.step4desc: If all the verses are considered transcribed correctly, you do not need to click each row separately to indicate that all transcription is correct. Just click the "Correct transcription" button and all lines will be marked as correctly transcribed on the right.
steps.step5desc: Each file can be saved after transcribing the first verse in the form of hOCR, text or TEI format with coordinates.
steps.step6desc: In the workspace, you can navigate to the next files using the navigation on the right: "Previous file", "Next file".
steps.step1extra_1: - allows you to swap sides of both windows.
steps.step1extra_2: - allows you to hide one window in favor of expanding the other and vice versa.
steps.step3extra_2: OCR software is not as effective as a human, so in doubtful cases (difficulty reading the text) and in order to avoid errors, it is always worth verifying the OCR result.

howToTranscribe.descPoint1: Global tools for working with text
howToTranscribe.descPoint2: Tools for working with the source file
howToTranscribe.descPoint3: Tools for working with text layers
howToTranscribe.instruction_1: The Historical Text Recognition Service provides users with tools to improve the processing of documents into digital text. In this way, it is possible to perform, for example, transcription (manual or with the help of automatic character recognition), translation or transliteration.
howToTranscribe.instruction_2: The results of working with the text can then be published on the site, thus creating a digital database of historical documents that can be searched for and viewed by other users.
howToTranscribe.instruction_3: A special workspace is used to implement projects, into which users upload document source files and perform various types of text conversions. Projects can be carried out independently or as a team.
howToTranscribe.instruction_4: Thanks to the possibility of creating multiple text layers, you can create e.g. transcription and translation of the source document at the same time. In addition to entering text into layers, the user has the ability to import text files, mark elements of the logical structure (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, etc.), as well as build indexes of passwords, places and people.
howToTranscribe.instruction_5: The results of the work can be shared with other members of the VTL community - by publishing the project on the site - but it can also be exported for private use.

howToVerify.title: How to verify?
howToVerify.desc: The task of the transcription verifier is to check the transcription for correctness and quality of the text.

section.howToAssignRole: How do you assign a verifier role to a user?
section.verificationDescription1: Verifier tools in the transcription window. The verifier has all the tools transscribers and developers have in the transcription window. In addition, the verifier has more options by marking the correctness of row verification. Transcription validation by the transcript:
section.verificationDescription2: How to select a correctly verified row?
section.verificationDescription3: After verifying the transcription, the transcript will no longer have the rights to edit the transcribed content. Only the creator and verifier will have such functionality.
section.howToStart_desc: You can enter moderation mode both from the details of your own project and from the workspace, where you can work with text:
section.howToAssignRole_desc: The user who created the project is assigned the Administrator role, which gives them both participant and moderator privileges for the project. As an administrator, you can moderate the changes yourself or you can assign this role to another user - without losing it yourself. Here's how:

assignRolesSteps.step1: The transcription verifier is designated by its creator. The creator can verify his transcription himself or assign the role of verifier to the person to whom he shared the object. The author sets such permissions on the Privileges tab on the My Transcription page.
assignRolesSteps.step2: Verifier role assignment. Users who have access to the object have a transcript role by default, which means that by default they only have access to the creator object. For a selected person to be able to verify an object, their role must be changed to Verifier.
assignRolesSteps.step2desc: When you add another user to your project, you are automatically assigned a participant role that gives you the ability to edit text layers. To change the role, expand the menu in the table next to its/its data and select the role: Moderator.
assignRolesSteps.step1desc: This tab is located on the details page of the project you created. There you can add project participants, check and change their role, as well as get acquainted with the statistics of the work of individual participants.

startVeryficationSteps.step1: To verify, click the Transcription Verification tab on the My Transcription page.
startVeryficationSteps.step2: Select the page you want to verify from the list and click the Verify button. A transcription window will open, where you will be able to verify the transcribed text.
startVeryficationSteps.step2desc: The ability to change modes is in the drop-down menu, located in the top bar of the workspace - next to the file name
startVeryficationSteps.step1desc: In the Moderation view there is a table in which, in addition to summarizing the number of areas in the state: "For approval", "Accepted" and "Rejected", there is a link to the Moderation Mode.
